item.text:
# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan (2024): 3B.2 evidence note

Bottom line: **strongly negative overall**. I found extensive evidence of toleration or continuation of abusive conduct by police and other state bodies, especially against political opponents and Ahmadis. I found **no convincing 2024 evidence** that Sharif punished abusive officers or clearly intervened to stop those abuses. The only favorable material is indirect: he did call for justice and order after major attacks, but not for accountability for state abuse.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Slightly favorable, indirect | High level emergency meeting chaired by the honourable PM on 27 March 2024 | Press Information Department, Pakistan | 2024-03-27 | https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/24838 | After the Besham attack on Chinese nationals, Sharif convened a high-level meeting, condemned the killing of civilians, and said the perpetrators would be brought to justice swiftly. This shows a willingness to call for accountability in the abstract, but it does not directly address police, military, intelligence, or prison abuse. | 3B.2; also 3B.1 |
| Negative | Pakistan: Election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on people’s rights | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/ | Amnesty called the election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown a blunt rights violation during an intense crackdown on the opposition. This is direct evidence that the authorities tolerated coercive state abuse around the elections. | 3B.2; also 3B.1, 2B.6 |
| Negative | Pakistan Government Intensifies Crackdown on Political Dissent | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-09 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent | HRW reported over 500 arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and mobile internet cuts during the PTI march, with many people arrested for peaceful protest and some charged under vague public-order laws. That is strong evidence of tolerating abusive policing and mass arrests. | 3B.2; also 3B.1 |
| Negative | Pakistani police detain two parliamentarians in swoop on ex-PM Khan's party | Reuters / ThePrint | 2024-09-10 | https://theprint.in/world/pakistani-police-detain-two-parliamentarians-in-swoop-on-ex-pm-khans-party/2260202/ | Police detained PTI parliamentarians in late-night swoops after a rally demanding Khan’s release. The detentions were described as illegal by PTI and had no contemporaneous public justification showing abuse was being restrained or corrected. | 3B.2 |
| Negative | Pakistan police detain several lawmakers of jailed Imran Khan's party | Reuters / ThePrint | 2024-09-10 | https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-police-detain-several-lawmakers-of-jailed-imran-khans-party/2260575/ | Reuters reported police raids on PTI lawmakers and leaders, with detentions following a major rally and no immediate official statement on charges. This supports a pattern of political policing rather than accountability. | 3B.2; also 3B.1 |
| Negative | Pakistan: Authorities Must Immediately Release Imran Khan From Arbitrary Detention | Amnesty International | 2024-09-11 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa33/8507/2024/en/ | Amnesty said Khan’s detention reflected fair-trial violations and weaponization of the legal system to keep him out of politics. This is direct evidence of tolerating abusive imprisonment and politically motivated detention. | 3B.2; also 3B.1 |
| Negative | Escalating attacks on minority Ahmadiyya community in Pakistan must end | Amnesty International | 2024-06-21 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/ | Amnesty documented 36 arbitrary arrests/detentions, dozens of police harassment cases, and orders barring Ahmadi rites, while authorities failed to ensure safety. This is strong evidence of state-body abuse and tolerance of discriminatory enforcement. | 3B.2; also 3B.1 |
| Negative | Pakistan: Authorities must end escalating attacks on minority Ahmadiyya community | Amnesty International | 2024-06-21 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/ | The article adds that district authorities issued preventive detentions and that police and provincial governments acted extrajudicially across the country. It is the clearest 2024 evidence of authorities tolerating abuse by police and district officials. | 3B.2; also 3B.1 |
| Negative | Pakistan. Les autorités doivent mettre fin à l’escalade des attaques visant la minorité ahmadie | Amnesty International | 2024-06-21 | https://www.amnesty.org/fr/latest/news/2024/06/pakistan-authorities-must-end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/ | Same factual record as above: arbitrary arrests, police harassment, and orders blocking Ahmadi religious rites. This reinforces that abusive local state conduct was not being meaningfully checked. | 3B.2; also 3B.1 |
| Negative | Pakistan Government Intensifies Crackdown on Political Dissent | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-09 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2117503.html | HRW’s summary adds that police used tear gas, blocked roads, and conducted arrests in a crackdown on PTI dissent. It supports the conclusion that Sharif’s government tolerated coercive police conduct against opponents. | 3B.2; also 3B.1 |
| Negative | Pakistan: Authorities must end ongoing injustice of civilian trials by military courts | Amnesty International | 2026-05-07 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2026/05/pakistan-authorities-must-end-ongoing-injustice-of-civilian-trials-by-military-courts/ | This is a later source, so not 2024 evidence, but it describes December 2024 military-court convictions of 105 protesters from the 9 May protests, showing the abusive legal pattern continued late in Sharif’s term. I am noting it as background only, not as a primary 2024 claim. | 3B.2; also 3B.1 |

## Synthesis

- Best-supported conclusion: Sharif’s 2024 record shows **tolerance of abusive state conduct**, not meaningful restraint or punishment.
- The clearest patterns are:
  - political crackdown on PTI and opposition figures,
  - arbitrary detention and military-court style coercion,
  - police harassment and preventive detentions of Ahmadis,
  - failure to prevent or punish mob-linked and district-level abuses,
  - repression through internet shutdowns and public-order measures.
- I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that Sharif disciplined police, intelligence services, prison officials, military personnel, or party loyalists for abusive conduct.
- The only mildly favorable material is procedural, not substantive: a condolence meeting after the Besham attack, with a promise of swift justice, but that does not show accountability for state abuse.

## Search gap

- I did **not** find a 2024 source showing Sharif punished officers for torture, disappearances, unlawful killings, or prisoner abuse.
- I did **not** find evidence of a public accountability mechanism that corrected abusive policing or intelligence conduct in 2024.
- So the record is best summarized as **toleration plus weak or absent accountability**, with no strong countervailing evidence.
